Earlier gameplay summary (agent-written, uncertain claims remain uncertain):
CURRENT GOAL/STATE: Solve puzzle 1-5-2, then continue set 1-5. Level select previously showed 1-1 through 1-4 checked complete, 1-5 unlocked, and 3.0% overall progress. 1-5-1 was solved by a direct circle-to-square horizontal route, filling all four indicators. In 1-5-2 (3x3), circle=r1c1, star=r1c3, triangle=r3c1, square=r3c3; rows are top-to-bottom and columns left-to-right. The latest completed moves drew the full-grid route r3c3→r3c1→r2c1→r2c3→r1c3→r1c1. Thus it starts at the square, visits the triangle then star, and ends at the circle. It has not yet been submitted in the supplied history. Immediately before its last segment, square/triangle/star were filled and circle was still unfilled; latest visual state after reaching the circle was not separately reported.

CONTROLS/OBSERVED MECHANICS: Click a level panel to open it. Drag from an endpoint to start a path; buttonless pointer movement extends it orthogonally, including across several cells in one move. Left-click submits an active completed route. Right-click reliably resets the current route. A rejected route can remain visible and stop responding to extension. Visited symbols become filled. Successful routes have been noncrossing. Solved puzzles fill the bottom indicator(s) and make the right arrow solid green; that arrow advances. A solid green right star generally ends a set/returns toward level select. Some top-right square/X controls produced no visible effect during one early rejected puzzle, so their functions remain unclear.

COMPLETED SETS/LEARNED RULES: 1-1: ordinary routes were drawn circle→square and left-click submitted. Puzzle 1-1-4 additionally required visiting star and triangle waypoints. 1-2: accepted routes ran from the square toward the boxed circle and visited required symbols. In 1-2-1, circle→square was rejected, while square→circle made the dashed goal border solid and was accepted. In 1-2-2, a forward perimeter route through all four corner circles to the central square was rejected; the reverse, starting at the central square and ending at the boxed top-left circle, succeeded. 1-2-3 and 1-2-4 likewise succeeded square→boxed circle through all triangles.

1-3: Early puzzles accepted routes through downward triangles while excluding upward triangles, but this is not a universal rule. In 1-3-4, the route r1c1→r1c5→r3c5→r3c1→r5c1→r5c5 collected every downward triangle and avoided upward triangles; square→circle was rejected, while the identical reverse circle→square route was accepted. In 1-3-5, an initial probe from the top-left circle entered an apparently enclosed corridor and was reset. The accepted route instead ran from the top-right circle to the bottom-right square via r1c9→r1c7→r3c7→r3c9→r4c9→r4c8→r5c8→r5c3→r6c3→r6c2→r8c2→r8c6→r9c6→r9c9. It collected four downward triangles, avoided every upward triangle, and left the top-left circle and left-side triangles unvisited, proving not every visible symbol is always mandatory.

1-4: Evidence showed all triangles were required in these puzzles. In 1-4-1, bypassing the upward triangle filled only two of three indicators; a detour visiting both triangles succeeded. 1-4-2 through 1-4-4 also succeeded by visiting every triangle. In 1-4-5, a full five-row snake through all fifteen triangles and both endpoints was rejected square→circle with only the third indicator filled; the identical reverse circle→boxed-square snake succeeded. 1-4-6 required a noncrossing route from the bottom-right circle through both circles and all thirteen triangles, ending at the boxed bottom-left square; it succeeded. Therefore boxed/dashed endpoints are not a reliable universal start indicator, and exact route direction can matter.

1-5-2 FAILED TESTS (all covered every grid cell and connected all four symbols): (A) Forward r1c1→r3c1→r3c2→r1c2→r1c3→r3c3, visiting triangle before star, filled the first three of four indicators but not the fourth. Its reverse, r3c3→r1c3→r1c2→r3c2→r3c1→r1c1, filled only the third indicator. (B) Forward row-wise snake r1c1→r1c3→r2c3→r2c1→r3c1→r3c3, visiting star before triangle, again filled only the first three indicators. Hovering the empty fourth indicator produced no visible tooltip or other useful change. The currently drawn route is the reverse of B, the remaining untested direction/order combination.

UNRESOLVED: The fourth indicator’s rule is unknown. The hypothesis that merely visiting star before triangle is sufficient was disproven by forward B. Reversing a complete route helped in earlier sets but already failed for reverse A here, so direction alone is not a general explanation. Indicator patterns are observed evidence; interpretations about waypoint order or hidden requirements remain guesses. Useful current 3x3 cell centers observed earlier: columns x≈0.399/0.500/0.600 and rows y≈0.318/0.500/0.682; right advance control is around x=0.958,y=0.500 when active.
